clinicalPearls: RCDP1 is an autosomal recessive peroxisomal disorder caused by biallelic PEX7 variants; PEX7 is the cytosolic receptor for the peroxisomal targeting signal type 2 (PTS2), so its loss impairs import of a specific subset of peroxisomal enzymes.

The biochemical signature is deficient plasmalogen (ether phospholipid) synthesis together with impaired phytanic acid alpha-oxidation, while very-long-chain fatty acid oxidation and beta-oxidation remain intact, distinguishing it from Zellweger spectrum disorders.

Classic features are symmetrical rhizomelic (proximal) shortening of the limbs, congenital cataracts, a characteristic dysmorphic facies, profound growth and psychomotor retardation, and progressive contractures.
Radiographs show punctate epiphyseal and extra-epiphyseal calcific stippling (chondrodysplasia punctata) and coronal clefts of the vertebral bodies, which fade over the first years of life.
PTS2-dependent enzymes affected include alkyl-dihydroxyacetone-phosphate synthase (plasmalogen synthesis), phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase (phytanic acid oxidation) and peroxisomal 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase.

Biochemical diagnosis rests on markedly reduced erythrocyte plasmalogens with raised plasma phytanic acid (often normal in the newborn period until dietary phytanate accumulates) and normal very-long-chain fatty acids.
A milder, non-rhizomelic phenotype with longer survival and residual plasmalogen synthesis occurs with hypomorphic PEX7 alleles, broadening the clinical spectrum.
Epilepsy, recurrent respiratory infections, feeding difficulty and cervical spinal stenosis contribute substantially to morbidity.
reference.pathophysiology: PEX7 encodes the soluble cytosolic receptor that recognises the peroxisomal targeting signal type 2 (a cleavable N-terminal nonapeptide) and, in cooperation with PEX5L, delivers PTS2-bearing matrix enzymes into intact, structurally normal peroxisomes. In RCDP1 loss of functional PEX7 selectively blocks import of this small group of enzymes while peroxisome assembly and PTS1-dependent import (including most very-long-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation) proceed normally. Two consequences dominate. First, the enzymes of ether phospholipid (plasmalogen) synthesis, particularly alkyl-dihydroxyacetone-phosphate synthase, fail to reach the peroxisome, so plasmalogens, which are abundant structural lipids of myelin, cell membranes and surfactant and function as antioxidants, are severely deficient; this underlies the neurological, ocular and skeletal pathology. Second, phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase is mislocalised, impairing alpha-oxidation so that dietary phytanic acid accumulates over time and adds a toxic burden. The skeletal dysplasia reflects disturbed endochondral ossification with abnormal calcium deposition in cartilage producing epiphyseal stippling and defective growth-plate function that causes the striking rhizomelic limb shortening. Inheritance is autosomal recessive, and residual receptor activity from hypomorphic alleles correlates with milder, non-rhizomelic disease and longer survival.
additionalDifferentials: Zellweger spectrum disorders and other peroxisome biogenesis defects (PEX1 and related genes)
RCDP types 2 and 3 (GNPAT and AGPS defects affecting plasmalogen synthesis directly)
Brachytelephalangic (X-linked recessive) chondrodysplasia punctata from ARSE/ARSL deficiency
Warfarin embryopathy and maternal vitamin K deficiency causing stippled epiphyses
Maternal autoimmune disease or vitamin B12 deficiency associated chondrodysplasia punctata
Other skeletal dysplasias with rhizomelia such as achondroplasia group disorders
additionalInvestigations: Erythrocyte plasmalogen levels (reduced) and the plasmalogen precursor ratio
Plasma phytanic acid (raised, age-dependent) with normal very-long-chain fatty acids
PEX7 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis and enable carrier/prenatal testing
Skeletal survey for epiphyseal stippling, rhizomelic shortening and coronal vertebral clefts
Brain MRI for myelination and any migrational or progressive white-matter changes
Cervical spine imaging to assess for stenosis and instability
redFlags: Congenital cataracts with proximal limb shortening in a neonate, prompting urgent peroxisomal evaluation
Respiratory compromise from recurrent aspiration or infection
Cervical cord compression from spinal stenosis or instability
Refractory seizures or acute neurological deterioration
Failure to thrive with severe feeding difficulty
reference.prognosis: Classic RCDP1 carries a poor prognosis with most severely affected children dying in infancy or early childhood, commonly from respiratory complications, though some survive into the early school years; milder non-rhizomelic variants have longer survival with less severe disability. Management is supportive and multidisciplinary, as no curative therapy exists.
pitfalls: Relying on plasma phytanic acid in the newborn period, when it may be normal before dietary accumulation, and missing the diagnosis
Confusing RCDP with Zellweger spectrum disorders despite the normal very-long-chain fatty acids and intact peroxisome assembly in RCDP
Overlooking non-genetic phenocopies such as warfarin embryopathy or maternal autoimmune disease causing stippling
Attributing all chondrodysplasia punctata to a single gene rather than distinguishing the RCDP subtypes and X-linked forms
Failing to monitor for cervical spinal stenosis, which can cause preventable neurological deterioration
references: Standard metabolic medicine and peroxisomal disorder references
Clinical genetics and dysmorphology reference texts
management: Supportive multidisciplinary care as no therapy corrects the PEX7 import defect, with anticonvulsants for seizure control
Dietary restriction of phytanic acid to reduce accumulated phytanate once dietary intake begins
Aggressive treatment of respiratory infections and ventilatory support, since respiratory complications are the leading cause of death
Nutritional support and gastrostomy feeding for feeding difficulty and faltering growth
Cataract surgery and ophthalmological follow-up for the congenital cataracts
Physiotherapy and orthopaedic management of progressive contractures and scoliosis
Genetic counselling with carrier and prenatal testing for this autosomal recessive PEX7 disorder
Early palliative-care involvement in the classic severe phenotype
